newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares slip with Wall St in late trade.
newsitem.headline: German shares slip with Wall St in late trade.

text.p: German shares lost steam on Monday, dragged lower in late trade by a weak start on Wall Street as the momentum that drove prices to new records last week wore off amid low turnover.
The DAX index closed bourse dealings down 9.64 points at 3,785.77 points at mid-afternoon, while the IBIS DAX slipped further to close down 43.03 points at 3,766.89 in post-bourse computer dealings.

But while the DAX slipped further from the psychologically crucial 3,800-point level, some dealers remained optimistic for the DAX to climb above 4,000 points in second half of 1997 after the index rose 31 percent in the first half.

Low interest rates and stable inflation, along with favourable profit developments from many major German companies and strong demand for shares, will continue to underpin the market in the second half of the year, some dealers said.
Among specific shares on Monday, chemical and automotive stocks were mainly firmer than the broader market.
Luxury carmaker Porsche was a top percentage gainer, rising 190 marks to 2,320 marks in bourse trade due to the stronger dollar, while Volkswagen gained 32 marks to 1,337 marks.

Chemical group Bayer AG ended up two pfennigs at 67.02 marks, while Hoechst AG gained 1.38 marks to 73.98 marks after the group said it would take a breather on acquisitions in its pharmaceuticals division.
